heading: GDP per person in six countries
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 1 with buttons for the vertical scale and a menu of countries
plot_title: 2022: U.S. income per person 5× South Africa's; China's up 24-fold since 1950
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [Maddison Project Database 2023, GDP per capita (`gdppc`), Groningen Growth and Development Centre](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/historicaldevelopment/maddison/releases/maddison-project-database-2023) (Bolt and van Zanden 2024, [doi:10.34894/INZBF2](https://doi.org/10.34894/INZBF2)), converted from 2011 to 2022 dollars with the
[U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis GDP deflator (`A191RD3A086NBEA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/A191RD3A086NBEA), via FRED.
Country groups: [World Bank country classifications](https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/906519-world-bank-country-and-lending-groups).
Prepared files: [`data/ch01/fig1-1.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/fig1-1.csv), [`data/ch01/maddison_world.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/maddison_world.csv) and [`data/ch01/countries.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/countries.csv)
(see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 1.1 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: The U.S. employment-population ratio
plot_title: The ratio fell 4.5 points in 2007–09 and 9.9 points in the Covid-19 recession
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey, Employment-Population Ratio (`EMRATIO`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/EMRATIO), via FRED;
recession dates: [NBER business cycle dates](https://www.nber.org/research/business-cycle-dating), as in [the NBER-based recession indicator (`USREC`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/USREC), via FRED.
Prepared files: [`data/ch01/fig1-2.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/fig1-2.csv) and [`data/ch01/recessions.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/recessions.csv)
(see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 1.2 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: Inflation rates in certain rich countries
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 3 with a menu of countries
plot_title: Inflation peaked in the 1970s (24% in the U.K.) and surged again in 2021–22
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [World Bank, World Development Indicators, Inflation, consumer prices (`FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG`)](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG), also via FRED for the
[United Kingdom (`FPCPITOTLZGGBR`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FPCPITOTLZGGBR), the [euro area (`FPCPITOTLZGEMU`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FPCPITOTLZGEMU) and [Japan (`FPCPITOTLZGJPN`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FPCPITOTLZGJPN);
United States: [U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (`CPIAUCNS`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCNS), via FRED;
gaps filled from the [World Bank's Global Inflation Database](https://www.worldbank.org/en/research/brief/inflation-database)
(Ha, Kose and Ohnsorge). Country groups: [World Bank country classifications](https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/906519-world-bank-country-and-lending-groups).
Prepared files: [`data/ch01/fig1-3.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/fig1-3.csv), [`data/ch01/inflation_world.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/inflation_world.csv) and [`data/ch01/countries.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/countries.csv)
(see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 1.3 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: Budget and trade deficits in the United States
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 5 with a menu of countries (the G20 and OECD members)
plot_title: U.S. budget deficit near 14% of GDP in 2020; trade deficit peaked in 2006
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, national accounts, via FRED: [federal government net saving (`FGDEF`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FGDEF), [net exports (`NETEXP`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/NETEXP) and [GDP (`GDP`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDP);
other countries: [IMF, World Economic Outlook, general government net lending/borrowing (`GGXCNL_NGDP`)](https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/GGXCNL_NGDP) and
[World Bank, World Development Indicators, External balance on goods and services (`NE.RSB.GNFS.ZS`)](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NE.RSB.GNFS.ZS). Country groups: [World Bank country classifications](https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/906519-world-bank-country-and-lending-groups).
Prepared files: [`data/ch01/fig1-5.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/fig1-5.csv), [`data/ch01/deficits_world.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/deficits_world.csv) and [`data/ch01/countries.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/countries.csv)
(see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 1.5 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: Per capita GDP in the United States
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 7 with a menu of countries (the G20 and OECD members)
plot_title: United States: GDP per person grew 1.9% a year, 1870–2025
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED: [real GDP (`GDPCA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDPCA), [population (`B230RC0A052NBEA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/B230RC0A052NBEA)
and [GDP deflator (`A191RD3A086NBEA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/A191RD3A086NBEA); [Congressional Budget Office, Real Potential GDP (`GDPPOT`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDPPOT), via FRED;
before 1929 and for other countries: [Maddison Project Database 2023, GDP per capita (`gdppc`), Groningen Growth and Development Centre](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/historicaldevelopment/maddison/releases/maddison-project-database-2023) (Bolt and van Zanden 2024, [doi:10.34894/INZBF2](https://doi.org/10.34894/INZBF2))
(the textbook uses the Barro-Ursúa data before 1929).
Prepared files: [`data/ch01/fig1-7.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/fig1-7.csv) and [`data/ch01/maddison_world.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/maddison_world.csv)
(see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch01/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 1.7 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)
